movesets.name: Choice Specs
movesets.description:
Leveraging its high Special Attack and good coverage, Choice Specs Iron Crown is a strong wallbreaker that can 2HKO a number of the metagame's defensive options like Garganacl and Gliscor. Tachyon Cutter being a multi-hit move lets Iron Crown OHKO Focus Sash Glimmora without activating Toxic Debris, break Multiscale on Dragonite, and deal significant damage to Landorus-T. Psyshock is preferred to let Iron Crown take on specially defensive walls like Galarian Slowking, Clodsire, and Blissey, while Psychic Noise can be used instead to prevent Pokemon like Corviknight and Zapdos from healing in front of it. Volt Switch lets Iron Crown pivot out of Pokemon it would otherwise struggle against while also dealing significant damage to the likes of Primarina and Alomomola. Focus Blast helps Iron Crown deal with Steel-types like Kingambit and Iron Treads and is its best option to damage Ting-Lu. Tera Steel increases the power of Tachyon Cutter, letting it 2HKO offensive Gholdengo variants and OHKO fully HP invested Landorus-T most of the time, while Tera Fighting Focus Blast guarantees a 2HKO on Ting-Lu, as well as OHKOes Ogerpon-W most of the time and guarantees an OHKO on Cinderace. Both Tera types also remove Iron Crown's weakness to Dark-type moves, improving its matchup against offensive Dark-types like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott.

Choice Specs Iron Crown needs physically offensive teammates like Zamazenta and Dragonite that can reliably remove specially defensive Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Blissey. In return, they benefit from Iron Crown being able to handle physical walls like Clefable and Dondozo. Because Iron Crown will be consistently locked into one move, it's easier to revenge kill, so it needs defensive teammates such as Primarina and Landorus-T that can switch into faster offensive Pokemon like Darkrai and Zamazenta while also providing pivot support for Iron Crown. Alomomola is another good teammate for Iron Crown, pivoting it into favorable matchups and keeping it healthy with Wish. Gholdengo is especially annoying for Iron Crown, as it resists both of its STAB moves and can easily heal off damage, so teammates like Kingambit and Great Tusk that can easily take care of it are useful. Finally, Iron Crown benefits from entry hazard setters like Hisuian Samurott that can soften up foes and allow it to clean them up easier.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
Assault Vest Iron Crown serves as a strong offensive pivot and sturdy check to a bevy of special attackers like Calm Mind Iron Valiant, Kyurem, and Enamorus. Tachyon Cutter's multi-hit properties allow it to bypass Glimmora's Focus Sash to OHKO it before it can set up any entry hazards. Future Sight's delayed damage puts a tremendous amount of pressure on the opposing team, since Dark-types switching in to block Future Sight or Steel-types and special walls trying to sponge the attack will have to survive powerful physical attacks from teammates like Great Tusk, Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, Zamazenta, and Weavile; Psychic Noise offers lower but more immediate damage while simultaneously nullifying recovery attempts from Gholdengo, Blissey, Corviknight, Garganacl, and Clodsire, allowing Iron Crown and its teammates to force significant damage against these threats. Focus Blast rounds out Iron Crown's coverage by hitting Kingambit, Ting-Lu, and Tera Steel Clodsire super effectively, and it is also its strongest attack against opposing Iron Crown. Volt Switch allows Iron Crown to capitalize on its ability to force out most special attackers and gain momentum for its team and has great synergy with Future Sight by safely pivoting in the aforementioned powerful physical attackers that can take advantage of the chip damage or switches it forces. Assault Vest greatly boosts Iron Crown's special bulk, allowing it to better handle special attackers like Calm Mind Iron Valiant and Enamorus. Tera Fighting turns Iron Crown's weakness to Dark-type attacks into a resistance, allowing it to survive Kingambit's Sucker Punch in a pinch while boosting its Focus Blast to 2HKO Ting-Lu and physically defensive Corviknight; Tera Fairy also offers a Dark resistance, but the Dragon immunity, Fighting resistance, and Fairy neutrality it provides allow Iron Crown to better check Dragapult and more reliably handle mixed and physical Iron Valiant sets without compromising its ability to check Calm Mind variants as heavily.

Iron Crown is best run on bulky offense teams, which can both cover Iron Crown's defensive shortcomings and maintain a similar level of offensive pressure, often in the form of additional pivoting options to maintain momentum. Hisuian Samurott is a spectacular teammate; it can form a VoltTurn core with Iron Crown using Flip Turn, reliably set Spikes with Ceaseless Edge, and even remove Heavy-Duty Boots with its strong STAB Knock Off to allow the duo to rack up massive amounts of lasting damage through Spikes and Future Sight or Psychic Noise. The two share excellent defensive synergy, as Hisuian Samurott's Ghost and Dark resistances cover Dragapult, Gholdengo, and opposing Hisuian Samurott while Iron Crown's Grass and Fairy resistances cover Rillaboom and Iron Valiant. Ceaseless Edge and Knock Off have impeccable synergy with Future Sight, and Hisuian Samurott's Razor Shell hits Dark-types like Ting-Lu and Kingambit very hard, rendering Iron Crown's Future Sight much more difficult to switch in against. Landorus-T is another great teammate; it also forms a powerful VoltTurn core with Iron Crown, can blanket check most physical attackers with Intimidate and Rocky Helmet to complement Iron Crown's ability to blanket check most special attackers with Assault Vest, can set up Stealth Rock, and the two also boast impeccable defensive synergy courtesy of Iron Crown checking Ice Beam users like Deoxys-S and Landorus-T checking physical Iron Valiant and Heatran. Together, Iron Crown, Hisuian Samurott, and Landorus-T form an extremely powerful core that resists every type in the game, utilizes multiple pivoting options, sets up both Stealth Rock and Spikes, and can blanket check many physical and special attackers alike. Calm Mind Primarina is a good teammate that can run Psychic Noise itself, allowing Iron Crown to more freely run Future Sight, and can take advantage of Iron Crown's ability to wear down teams over time to set up for a late-game sweep once threats like Encore Iron Valiant are dealt with. Physically defensive Moltres is another solid teammate, as it can reliably check most physical attackers by spreading burn with Will-O-Wisp and Flame Body and heavily punishes Dark-types like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott and Steel-types like Gholdengo aiming to switch into Future Sight, and appreciates Iron Crown's ability to temporarily keep special attackers like Deoxys-S and Walking Wake at bay. Kingambit itself makes for a strong teammate, as with Iron Crown's Future Sight support, Kingambit has a much easier time both finding opportunities to set up with Swords Dance and muscle past physical walls like Dondozo and Alomomola, which are quickly overwhelmed by the combination of Future Sight and powerful Dark-type attacks possibly boosted further by Black Glasses, Tera Dark, and Supreme Overlord. Kingambit additionally resists Ghost- and Dark-type attacks from the likes of Gholdengo and opposing Kingambit lacking Low Kick, which Iron Crown greatly appreciates. Zamazenta and Weavile also greatly appreciate both Iron Crown's Future Sight support and its pivoting capabilities, allowing them to be brought in safely and giving them opportunities to fire off a powerful Body Press or Knock Off that, when paired with Future Sight, can prove nearly impossible to switch in against.

movesets.name: Calm Mind
movesets.description:
With solid bulk, a one-time Speed boost, and near-perfect coverage, Calm Mind Iron Crown is a solid sweeper and late-game cleaner. Tachyon Cutter has the benefit of hitting twice, allowing Iron Crown to OHKO common Focus Sash leads in Glimmora and Ribombee, giving it an alternate use as an anti-lead that denies entry hazards. Tachyon Cutter also allows Iron Crown to break Substitutes while chipping the Pokemon hiding behind it; it can break Zamazenta’s Substitute after one Calm Mind and Kyurem’s without any Calm Mind boosts. After one Calm Mind, Iron Crown can hit several important ranges with Tachyon Cutter such as an OHKO on Kyurem and a good chance to KO offensive Landorus-T; it also secures a 2HKO against defensive Landorus-T variants while not being 2HKOed by Earth Power. The choice of Psychic-type STAB move depends on the team's needs: Psyshock targets the lower Defense of Galarian Slowking, Ogerpon-W, and Primarina, while Psychic Noise prevents walls such as Dondozo, Pecharunt, Alomomola, and Corviknight from spamming recovery to outlast Iron Crown. Stored Power is an option that can reach astonishing power levels, capable of breaking past almost any non-immune wall; however, it requires several turns of setup and has no benefit other than raw damage. Focus Blast complements Iron Crown's STAB combination by providing excellent neutral and super effective coverage against everything in the metagame except Gholdengo. It is Iron Crown's best way of hitting Ting-Lu and Steel-types like Kingambit and Iron Treads. The EV spread maximizes Iron Crown's offensive capabilities while letting Booster Energy enhance its Speed; the leftover EVs are invested into HP for increased survivability, notably allowing Iron Crown to survive a Choice Specs Kyurem Earth Power. Tera Fighting and Tera Fairy remove Iron Crown's original weaknesses, most notably both turning its weakness to Dark-type moves such as Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott’s Sucker Punch into a resistance to give it an easier time sweeping. Tera Fighting strengthens Iron Crown's Focus Blast, OHKOing Darkrai 2HKOing on Ting-Lu at +1. Tera Fairy is a more defensive Tera type that, unlike Tera Fighting, gives it fewer weaknesses. It further improves Iron Crown’s matchups against Walking Wake, Raging Bolt, and Dragapult by turning the Dragon resistance into an immunity.

Calm Mind Iron Crown best fits on offense teams that appreciate its unique traits as a sweeper. Due to its low initial damage output, Iron Crown will struggle against bulky threats such as Ting-Lu, Galarian Slowking, and Gholdengo, which require significant chip damage for it to break through them. Teammates such as Hisuian Samurott and Ogerpon-W significantly threaten these bulky foes, and in return, Iron Crown can deal with Kyurem and Rillaboom. Iron Crown is also extremely vulnerable to many offensive threats, many of which can survive almost any hit from an unboosted Iron Crown such as Hisuian Samurott, Landorus-T, and Kingambit; they can either force a Tera or outright KO Iron Crown. Ogerpon-W and Iron Moth also resist Tachyon Cutter and threaten a clean 2HKO on Iron Crown. As such, Iron Crown appreciates pivots such as Pecharunt, which walls Ogerpon-W and weakens it with Parting Shot, and Alomomola, which can take hits from Weavile, Hisuian Samurott, and other physical threats and threaten a burn with Scald to enable Iron Crown set up on them. Furthermore, special walls like Blissey and Clodsire using Tera Dark completely wall Iron Crown, as Focus Blast does insufficient damage. Because of this, Iron Crown appreciates physically offensive teammates, such as Hisuian Samurott, Great Tusk, and Zamazenta, that can deal with its checks; in return, they appreciate Iron Crown's removal of Fairy- and Fighting-type threats such as Enamorus, Hatterene, and Great Tusk. Hisuian Samurott and Great Tusk also set entry hazards to accumulate chip damage, which can compensate for this set's low initial power and allow Iron Crown to clean up or sweep earlier than expected.

movesets.name: Double Dance Sweeper (Psychic)
movesets.description:
Iron Crown is an amazing Stored Power setup sweeper for Psychic due to its access to multiple useful setup moves, like Calm Mind and Agility, and a type combination that lets it activate Weakness Policy easily. On top of that, its typing means it's immune to Toxic and also has important resistances to types such as Dragon and Fairy. Calm Mind and Agility allow Iron Crown to boost its stats and Stored Power while also punishing opponents that play passively, trying to stall out dual screens. Behind dual screens, Iron Crown survives attacks like Fiery Dance from Choice Specs Iron Moth, Earth Power from Life Orb Landorus, and Knock Off from Alolan Muk, allowing it to capitalize on its weaknesses by activating Weakness Policy and boosting the power of Stored Power. Additionally, after activating its Weakness Policy and using a single Agility, Iron Crown can take on walls like Skarmory and Galarian Slowking, OHKOing the former after Stealth Rock damage and 2HKOing the latter; similarly, in this position, it makes quick work of offensive foes like Choice Band Dragapult, Landorus-T, and Ogerpon-H and -W. Tachyon Cutter is a secondary move that is meant to hit foes that are immune to Stored Power, such as Alolan Muk and Meowscarada, and it also bypasses enemies with Focus Sash and Sturdy, such as Glimmora and Ogerpon-C, respectively. Focus Blast can be used in place of Tachyon Cutter or Calm Mind to hit Steel-type foes, which resist Stored Power, and Dark-type foes, which are immune to it. Once Weakness Policy is activated, Focus Blast can eliminate special walls such as Ting-Lu and Heatran after they are mildly chipped. However, it is considered risky, as Focus Blast can miss. A Timid nature is preferred, since it lets Iron Crown outspeed Choice Scarf Dragapult after an Agility. However, a Modest nature can also be considered, as it still outspeeds Choice Scarf Meowscarada after an Agility, and at +2 Special Attack, Iron Crown can OHKO Heatran.

Deoxys-S and Scream Tail set up entry hazards and dual screens, allowing Iron Crown to survive hits and set up successfully. Indeedee-M is immune to Ghost and sets Psychic Terrain for Iron Crown, shielding it from priority moves such as Ceruledge's Shadow Sneak and Hisuian Samurott's Sucker Punch. It also provides Healing Wish support to bring Iron Crown back into shape if it gets worn down. Galarian Slowking assists Iron Crown by spreading poison through Toxic Spikes or Toxic, pressuring bulky special walls such as Ting-Lu, while also providing pivoting with Chilly Reception. Hatterene prevents foes from setting up hazards, allowing Iron Crown to come in safely, and it can also help weaken Dark-types. Iron Boulder heavily damages special walls that trouble Iron Crown such as Heatran and Hisuian Goodra. Additionally, Iron Boulder checks Fire-type threats such as Ogerpon-H, Volcarona, and Cinderace while also dissuading Cinderace from using Court Change to steal dual screens. Choice Specs Flutter Mane overwhelms Iron Crown, but Choice Scarf Iron Boulder outspeeds it and removes it. Latios provides a switch-in to Ground-type moves thanks to its immunity to them, and it removes Dragon-type foes such as Garchomp and Walking Wake. Hoopa-U helps in removing Ghost-types such as Gholdengo and Flutter Mane. Slowbro chips opposing Fire-type threats such as Hisuian Arcanine while also burning physical attackers, such as Barraskewda and Choice Band Excadrill, and setup sweepers, like Dragonite and Scizor, with Scald. Armarouge removes Steel-type threats that resist Iron Crown's STAB moves, such as Forretress and Iron Treads, with the combination of Aura Sphere and Armor Cannon.

movesets.name: Choice Specs (Steel)
movesets.description:
Iron Crown provides Steel teams breathing room against Fighting matchups, threatening intimidating foes such as Okidogi, Great Tusk, and Urshifu-R. Tachyon Cutter takes out threats like Focus Sash Breloom and Mimikyu, which normally don't get OHKOed. Volt Switch makes Iron Crown a fast and offensive pivot, allowing it to pivot out of foes such as Gholdengo and Alolan Muk, which otherwise threaten a ton of damage. Volt Switch can also heavily dent Flying and Water teams, damaging foes like Pelipper and Skarmory. Psychic allows Iron Crown to handle Fighting-type Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Iron Hands, and Great Tusk. Focus Blast breaks through Ursaluna, Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Heatran, which are hard to deal with for Steel teams.

Corviknight and Skarmory provide Iron Crown with a keen immunity to Ground-type moves. Corviknight removes entry hazards and offers a slow pivot through U-turn, whereas Skarmory sets hazards and phazes setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Sneasler and Dragon Dance Dragonite. Archaludon handles physical attackers such as Ceruledge and Ogerpon-H and exerts pressure on Dark-type foes such as Meowscarada and Bisharp, which threaten Iron Crown. Archaludon also spreads Thunder Wave to slow down fast foes like Tornadus-T and Greninja and sets Stealth Rock. Heatran provides an immunity to Fire-type moves from Ninetales and Volcarona while also setting Stealth Rock. Gholdengo, due to Good as Gold, prevents foes such as Blissey and Sableye from slowing down Iron Crown through Thunder Wave and also provides a Fighting immunity. Hisuian Goodra, thanks to its sheer special bulk, provides a safe switch-in against strong special attacks from threats like Greninja and Moltres. Iron Treads removes hazards and threatens Ground-types Pokemon such as Garchomp, Landorus-I, and Gliscor. With the help of priority in Sucker Punch, Bisharp shoves off Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane and Dragapult. In return, Iron Crown deals with Toxapex, Okidogi, and Great Tusk.

movesets.name: Fast Calm Mind Sweeper
movesets.description:
• Iron Crown is one of the best sweepers of the tier that, thanks to Expanding Force, hits really hard even without boosts! With Booster Energy, Iron Crown outspeeds almost everything in the metagame, and while in Psychic Terrain, it can gain a significant advantage early-game or close games easily after Dark- and Steel-types in its path have been removed.

  • Tachyon Cutter hits harder than Expanding Force when Psychic Terrain isn't up and helps against snow teams, OHKOing Alolan Ninetales before it can set up Aurora Veil. Notably, its two-hit nature allows Iron Crown to remove Focus Sash Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Glimmora with one move.

  • Calm Mind makes Iron Crown hard to remove with special attackers, especially if it Terastallized, and also helps to KO bulkier Pokemon like Terastallized Assault Vest Iron Hands, Assault Vest Rillaboom, and Gholdengo.

  • The EV spread is made to get the boost in Speed with Quark Drive while getting the maximum Special Attack possible, and the bulk investment is used to take a Flare Blitz from Incineroar.

  • Iron Crown pairs perfectly with Indeedee-F by setting up Psychic Terrain, helping it set up Calm Mind with Follow Me, and enabling it with Helping Hand to pick up KOs on foes like Terastallized Ogerpon-W after a boost. Iron Crown appreciates Follow Me for setup, and for this reason, it's usually paired with Ogerpon-W or Ogerpon-H. Ogerpon-W helps in dealing with Landorus and Fire-types like Incineroar and Chi-Yu, which can threaten Iron Crown, while Ogerpon-H can remove Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit, which would otherwise prevent a sweep. Both Ogerpon formes can also threaten Ting-Lu, a foe that's otherwise hard to remove.

  • Landorus is another Pokemon that helps to remove Steel- and Fire-types. Tornadus is great too, since it threatens Rillaboom with Bleakwind Storm and makes sure that Iron Crown is always the fastest Pokemon by matching the Tailwind from opposing Tornadus and Roaring Moon.

  • Tera Psychic increases Expanding Force's damage output further, helping to get KOs and putting a lot of pressure on the opponent, especially after a Calm Mind. It also allows Iron Crown to take neutral damage from Landorus's Earth Power, Incineroar's Flare Blitz, and Ogerpon-H's Ivy Cudgel. Tera Dragon allows Iron Crown to wall both Ogerpon-W and Ogerpon-H's STAB moves and take neutral damage from Gholdengo's Shadow Ball and Dark-type moves from Kingambit and Chien-Pao. The added resistances are especially useful in the Rillaboom matchup, since the STAB boost from Tera Psychic isn't as relevant without Psychic Terrain.

  • 44 HP / 36 Def / 172 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Modest or Timid: This spread survives Jolly Punching Glove Urshifu-R's Tera Water Surging Strikes, and Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball if using Assault Vest.

strategies.overview:
• Iron Crown is an excellent choice for offensive teams looking to take advantage of the powerful move Expanding Force thanks to its well-rounded stats and access to Booster Energy. It performs best against frailer offensive teams consisting of Pokemon that do not resist Expanding Force, such as Tornadus, Landorus, and Urshifu-R.

  • Although it can be used as a sweeper early-game to soften opposing teams, it is usually better to save Iron Crown for the late-game when its checks have been sufficiently weakened for it to sweep.

  • Indeedee-F is by far Iron Crown's best teammate, offering role compression as a Psychic Terrain setter and redirector. Access to Helping Hand also further amplifies its partner's ridiculous damage output.

  • Iron Crown's best counters are Dark- and Steel-types, namely Incineroar, Kingambit, Archaludon, and Gholdengo, all of which resist both of Iron Crown's STAB moves.

  • Therefore, Iron Crown appreciates Pokemon that can help remove these threats consistently, such as Landorus, Entei, and Urshifu-R. In return, Iron Crown can pressure opposing Urshifu-R and Amoonguss.

  • Rillaboom is another noteworthy check, as it is able to safely pivot in and override Psychic Terrain, weakening Expanding Force significantly. Other Pokemon with access to Ice Spinner like Chien-Pao and Dragonite can also be used to remove Psychic Terrain.

  • Faster Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane serve as good checks as well, but they have to watch out for Follow Me from Indeedee-F as they are vulnerable to Tachyon Cutter.

movesets.name: Booster Energy
movesets.description:
• Expanding Force is Iron Crown's go-to STAB move, allowing it to devastate foes under Psychic Terrain.

  • Tachyon Cutter helps secure the OHKO on Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Whimsicott, which commonly hold Focus Sash.

  • Tera Water is a naturally good defensive typing that, when coupled with Tera Blast, gives Iron Crown an out against the aforementioned Dark- and Steel-type Pokemon, which otherwise counter it. Focus Blast can be used over Tera Blast to secure the OHKO on Kingambit, but is rather inconsistent and is unable to hit Gholdengo.

  • An alternative spread of 76 HP / 4 Def / 172 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe allows Iron Crown to outspeed Flutter Mane and Chien-Pao thanks to Speed Booster Energy.

  • This set can also be run with a Modest nature to maximize Iron Crown's damage output, at the risk of underspeeding opposing Pokemon in the same Speed tier such as Modest Landorus and both Urshifu formes.

movesets.name: Double Dance
movesets.description: The combination of Calm Mind and Agility, which lets Iron Crown outspeed almost the entire metagame after just one use, gives it the potential to be a deadly setup sweeper. Stored Power gives Iron Crown scaling damage, letting it 2HKO offensive threats like Iron Moth and Zamazenta after one Agility and OHKO them after one Calm Mind with some chip damage. Additionally, it lets Iron Crown 2HKO specially defensive Garchomp and RegenVest Iron Hands at +4, which can be easily achieved by letting its Weakness Policy activate. Furthermore, with one Agility boost and after Weakness Policy has activated or Calm Mind has been used twice, it lets Iron Crown OHKO even Psychic-resistant Pokemon like Corviknight and Gholdengo and 2HKO most RegenVest users, like Manaphy and Swampert. Iron Crown is heavily reliant on setup moves to perform its role, so it is easily shut down by Taunt, can be stopped by dedicated special walls like Blissey and Chansey, and needs teammates like Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-H that can handle them. A dual screens setter like Corviknight or Deoxys-S is appreciated to help Iron Crown with both activating its Weakness Policy and setting up safely. Bulky Dark-types like Mandibuzz and Kingambit give Iron Crown a lot of trouble, so teammates like Galvanize Kommo-o and Iron Hands are needed to remove them.

movesets.name: Psychic Terrain Sweeper
movesets.description: • EV spread gets a Speed boost from Quark Drive

strategies.overview:
Draft Order: Round 3 onwards

Price Range: 11-12 points

Tera Price Range: 13-14 points

Overview: Iron Crown is an offensive Steel-type with a variety of setup and attacking sets. Opponents need to respect Booster Energy's setup potential as well as Choice Specs's wallbreaking power, which gives Iron Crown an overwhelming offensive presence. This becomes even more potent with access to Terastallization, making its sets even more unpredictable and difficult to handle. Also, Iron Crown can act as a solid pivot with its typing and access to Volt Switch, enabling powerful offensive teammates. However, it lacks some of the utility expected from a Steel- or Psychic-type Pokemon, most notably entry hazards, requiring teammates to provide that utility. It also has a relatively shallow movepool and often relies on Terastallization for type coverage.
strategies.comments:
Common Roles

Setup Sweeper: Iron Crown will often use Booster Energy to boost its Speed alongside setup moves such as Calm Mind and Iron Defense for a late-game sweep. It can also boost its Special Attack and use Agility to outspeed foes.

Choice Item Attacker: This set is a great mix-up against opponents expecting a late-game setup sweeper. This allows Iron Crown to switch in multiple times and keep attacking, and it is often great when its STAB moves line up well in the matchup.

Pivot: Iron Crown can also make use of its good defensive typing and access to Volt Switch to pivot around foes. These pivot sets make use of Iron Crown's good Special Attack and powerful attacking moves to help make progress, and they commonly run Assault Vest or another defensive item to help check opposing threats.

Common Moves

Primary STAB Moves: Tachyon Cutter, Psyshock, Psychic, Psychic Noise

Setup Moves: Calm Mind, Agility, Iron Defense

Utility Moves: Substitute, Volt Switch

Coverage: Focus Blast, Air Slash, Tera Blast

Niche Moves

Future Sight: Future Sight is a great option when Iron Crown is paired with a strong Fighting-type to force guaranteed KOs against opposing teams that cannot take moves of both types at the same time. Volt Switch enables this strategy as well by letting Iron Crown take the initiative to respond to a switch and bring in whatever Pokemon that will ensure a KO in that sequence. Note that having Future Sight as Iron Crown's only Psychic-type STAB move may enable certain foes to switch into it much more freely. This makes it a good option on Assault Vest sets, which have the moveslot to spare.

Stored Power: Stored Power is mostly used on either Weakness Policy sets or sets with multiple setup moves. The immediate power of other STAB moves typically makes them easier to use.

Common Items

Booster Energy: Booster Energy gives Iron Crown an immediate stat boost, ideally in Speed, to either force KOs or force out foes and enable it to set up safely. Pairing Speed boosting with special setup and vice versa gives it a lot of potency as a late-game sweeper.

Choice Specs / Choice Scarf: Choice items are quite useful on Iron Crown, leveraging its high Special Attack to immediately threaten foes. The significance of using a Choice item over Booster Energy is that Iron Crown can switch out and still see the same level of power or Speed throughout the match.

Assault Vest: Assault Vest is a good option on a pivot set to enable Iron Crown to take more hits and stick around longer, utilizing Volt Switch to pivot safely to a teammate without sustaining much damage itself.

Niche Items

Resistance Berries: Resistance Berries allow Iron Crown to trade favorably with certain foes and catch them off guard, but it often loses a lot of its value without an item to boost its stats.

Weakness Policy: Weakness Policy is an alternative way to boost Iron Crown's stats and can be paired with Agility to make Iron Crown a powerful offensive threat. However, this setup is less consistent than Booster Energy, requiring a super effective hit to come online.

Leftovers: Leftovers is a good choice on bulkier Iron Crown sets with Calm Mind, enabling it to stay healthy against more passive teams.

Tera

Iron Crown can benefit from being a Tera Captain, but it doesn't necessarily need it. This Pokemon is often drafted for its Steel typing, and it doesn't need Terastallization to function as much as some high-tier Tera Captains. That being said, if it is made a Captain, there are some notable benefits. The additional coverage from Tera Blast is often crucial for breaking through bulky Pokemon that resist its STAB moves. The other significant reason to make Iron Crown a Tera Captain is its low price point. It can be paired with other strong Tera Captains that cost 14-15 points, creating a nightmare for opponents to prepare for. Tera Ghost, Fire, and Fighting are all excellent offensive Tera types. Terastallizing into typings such as Water, Dragon, and Fairy can also give Iron Crown the defensive utility it often needs to set up freely.

Draft Strategy

Above all else, Iron Crown teams need to fill in utility roles elsewhere. Many typical drafts find a lot of their utility in Steel- and Psychic-type Pokemon, which Iron Crown simply doesn't provide. It is also important to play to Iron Crown's strengths by pairing up with strong offensive partners, so one teammate can enable the other.

Entry Hazard Setters: Iron Crown appreciates additional chip damage from entry hazards to help it wallbreak or sweep. Pokemon such as Garchomp, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu are excellent partners in this role.

Fighting-types / Physical Attackers: A physical attacker, particularly a Fighting-type, is a great option to pair with Iron Crown offensively. The duo can cover each other's weaknesses, with one enabling the other depending on the matchup. Pokemon such as Great Tusk, both Urshifu formes, and Sneasler can often fill this role well. Iron Crown also forms an effective VoltTurn core with Meowscarada, both Urshifu formes, and Sneasler, forcing a lot of chip damage and making positioning easier.

Strong Secondary Tera Captains: If Iron Crown is chosen as a Tera Captain, it often wants a teammate around the 14-15 point price range that can benefit a lot from Terastallization as well to force preparation. Pokemon such as Iron Moth, Keldeo, Ceruledge, Annihilape, and Ogerpon-C are excellent choices.

Frail Wallbreakers: Iron Crown can also use a pivot set to enable glass cannon teammates to enter the field safely. Pokemon such as Greninja, Darkrai, Enamorus, and Iron Bundle can all take advantage of this.

Checks and Counters

Steel- or Psychic-resistant Pokemon and Special Walls: Iron Crown often has trouble hitting several types of foes, including Dark-, Steel-, and Psychic-types. Pokemon such as Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, Jirachi, and Metagross can easily switch into its STAB moves. It often needs to rely on the inaccurate Focus Blast or set its Tera type to combat these foes.

Phazing: Given that Iron Crown often runs Booster Energy, many foes run phazing moves such as Roar and Whirlwind to stop its setup sets.

Fast Revenge Killers / Priority: Iron Crown's merely decent Speed often leaves it vulnerable to Choice Scarf users, and its Tera type needs to be selected carefully to let it take hits from priority moves. Pokemon such as Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Palafin can pose a threat to Iron Crown's setup.

movesets.name: Fast Weakness Policy
movesets.description:
• Fast Weakness Policy Iron Crown aims to switch up otherwise disadvantageous matchups such as Haxorus as well as Choice Band Ground-types such as Landorus-T by boosting itself with Iron Defense, then obtaining a Weakness Policy boost to threaten an OHKO on the next turn with Stored Power.
  • Tachyon Cutter is Iron Crown's best Steel-type STAB move, being able to immediately pressure Fairy-Type Pokemon such as Iron Valiant and Sylveon. Tachyon Cutter has other niches in breaking foes' Substitute, such as against SubSeed Ogerpon-W and Serperior.
  • Upon activation of Weakness Policy, Stored Power's Base Power increases by 80. Combined with any prior boosts Iron Crown may have obtained, this makes Stored Power its strongest Psychic-type STAB option.
  • Psyshock can be used to disrupt the matchup versus other Calm Mind users that resist Stored Power such as opposing Iron Crown and Cresselia, albeit using Psyshock may miss out on important KOs that Stored Power would otherwise obtain.
  • Psychic Noise may be used to prevent recovery moves from Pokemon such as Cresselia that would otherwise be able to deal with Iron Crown. Psychic Noise also deals additional damage to Iron Valiant and Alolan Ninetales compared to Iron Crown's other Psychic-type options.
  • Calm Mind is used in matchups versus special attacking Pokemon such as Primarina and Cresselia in order to boost up Iron Crown's Special Attack and Special Defense to a point where it does not take much damage from their attacks while threatening KOs with Tachyon Cutter and Stored Power.
  • The EVs are used to outspeed maximum Speed Haxorus and to tie the mirror matchup versus opposing Iron Crown. The bulk is meant to tank an Adamant Choice Band Great Tusk Headlong Rush after one Iron Defense.
  • An alternative EV spread of 96 HP / 112 Def / 48 SpA / 252 Spe with a Timid Nature can be used to have a slightly better chance against Donphan with Tachyon Cutter after a Weakness Policy boost while still surviving Choice Band Great Tusk's Headlong Rush. However, this makes Iron Crown less reliable into Choice Specs Primarina.

movesets.name: Defensive Weakness Policy
movesets.description:
• Defensive Weakness Policy Iron Crown uses Iron Defense and Calm Mind to boost its defenses to survive strong hits and KO back with Weakness Policy-boosted Stored Power.
  • Stored Power obtains a massive boost in Base Power when combined with Weakness Policy and stat-boosting moves.
  • Alternatively, Psyshock can be used for matchups Pokemon that have enough Special Defense to not be threatened by Stored Power, such as Cresselia and Pokemon that Iron Crown can't boost in front of like Iron Valiant.
  • Tachyon Cutter is hits Fairy-types such as Sylveon and Iron Valiant, and can break Substitute from Pokemon such as Serperior.
  • Calm Mind is used for matchups where boosting Special Attack and Special Defense is necessary, such as against Assault Vest Ursaluna-B.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Iron Crown to have a 75% chance to survive Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada's Knock Off in order to kill it with +2 Tachyon Cutter, as well as having favorable rolls to survive two Choice Band Ursaluna's Earthquake to boost with Iron Defense up to +4 and KO with Stored Power. The remaining EVs are placed in Speed for the mirror matchup and to base 50 speed Pokemon such as Ursaluna.
  • 36 Speed EVs can be used instead to outspeed Max Speed Primarina.
  • While this set is able to bulk many attacks, it is notably slower than faster Choice Band users like Landorus-T, making Defensive Iron Crown lose the matchup against them. Faster teammates that can deal with these Pokemon are ideal, such as attackers like Meowscarada.

movesets.name: Specially Defensive Weakness Policy
movesets.description:
• This specially defensive EV spread allows Weakness Policy Iron Crown to take special hits from very powerful special attackers such as Timid Choice Specs Darkrai, Raging Bolt, and Choice Specs Dragapult.
  • Psyshock is vital for matchups such as Calm Mind Raging Bolt, Iron Valiant, and Alolan Ninetales, as it helps hit the weaker physical side on the former and assists against Disable variants on the latter two.
  • The Defense EVs let Iron Crown survive Adamant Choice Band Knock Off from Meowscarada, while the Special Defense is enough to survive two Thunderbolts into a Thunderclap from Raging Bolt after a Calm Mind boost, since it would use Taunt on Iron Crown on the first turn. The Special Attack investment is enough to OHKO Haxorus with Tachyon Cutter after the Special Defense drop from Close Combat.
  • This Iron Crown set can struggle a lot against opposing Iron Crown due to the lack of Stored Power and matches up poorly against common Fire- and Ground-types and other miscellaneous threats like Hoopa-U and Corviknight, so it's recommended to utilize strong partners such as Air Balloon Volcanion and Ogerpon-W.

movesets.name: Special Attack Booster Energy
movesets.description:
• Calm Mind allows Iron Crown to compete with Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Cresselia, and opposing Iron Crown.
  • Psyshock enables Iron Crown to hit specially defensive foes, empowers it against Calm Mind users such as Weakness Policy Iron Crown and Clear Amulet Cresselia, and is important against Alolan Ninetales.
  • Tachyon Cutter exerts pressure on Fairy-type foes like Iron Valiant and Sylveon.
  • Focus Blast lets Iron Crown take on foes including Ursaluna-B and Hisuian Goodra. Alternatively, Psychic Noise can be used to check foes that rely on recovery moves, especially Pecharunt and Clear Amulet Cresselia. Moreover, Stored Power + Calm Mind allows Iron Crown to handle foes like Manaphy. Finally, Psychic allows Iron Crown to deal increased damage to foes such as Iron Hands and Speed Booster Energy Walking Wake.
  • The bulk EVs allow Iron Crown to survive Knock Off from Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada and Hydro Cannon from Timid Choice Specs Primarina, with the rest of the EVs being put into Special Attack.
  • Primarina is a great partner for Iron Crown, since Iron Crown is weak to Ground- Fire- and Dark-type attacks from foes like Landorus, Volcarona, and Urshifu-S; in return, Iron Crown provides an immunity to Poison. On top of this, Iron Crown's weakness to Ghost-type attacks can be remedied by using other Dark-types, such as Roaring Moon.

movesets.name: Speed Booster Energy
movesets.description:
• This set relies on outspeeding key threats such as Chien-Pao and Speed Booster Energy Great Tusk, using the Speed boost from Booster Energy to flip otherwise unfavorable matchups for Iron Crown.
  • Psychic is Iron Crown's strongest Psychic-type STAB move, which allows it to hit Pokemon like Iron Hands and Great Tusk. On the other hand, Psyshock is the best option against Pokemon like Raging Bolt, where both Pokemon typically use Calm Mind six times.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Iron Crown to tank an Earthquake from Adamant Choice Band Iron Hands and a Hydro Cannon from +3 Torrent Primarina at +4 Special Defense. The Speed EVs help it outspeed Porygon-Z, and the remaining EVs are invested in Special Attack.
  • Because Fire- and Dark-type Pokemon like Darkrai, Skeledirge, Hoopa-U, and Iron Moth are difficult for Iron Crown to deal with by itself, Primarina and Donphan work as good partners for Iron Crown.

movesets.name: Setup Sweeper
movesets.description:
Functioning as a niche setup sweeper, Iron Crown can leverage its good natural bulk and excellent coverage to effectively sweep. Psychic Noise is used to prevent healing from foes such as Gliscor and Moltres while being a more reliable STAB option when Iron Crown is not yet set up. As an alternative, Stored Power can be used in conjunction with Iron Defense in order to make Iron Crown a threatening Double Dance sweeper. Focus Blast is used to hit Steel-types such as Heatran and Ferrothorn, which could otherwise comfortably take its STAB moves. Tachyon Cutter is used to hit Fairy-types such as Hatterene and Tapu Lele, which would otherwise be able to switch in on Iron Crown. Iron Defense boosts the power of Stored Power while also making Iron Crown more resistant against physical attackers such as Zamazenta, Melmetal, and Dragonite, letting it turn them into setup fodder. 172 Special Attack EVs are used in order to grant Iron Crown Quark Drive's Speed boost with Booster Energy, letting it outspeed most foes.

This Iron Crown set fits exclusively on hyper offense teams where its ability to clean late-game is appreciated. Due to often lacking the bulk to set up reliably, dual screens support from teammates such as Zamazenta and Tapu Koko are appreciated, with the latter also activating its Quark Drive, potentially enabling Iron Crown to run a different item. Another good teammate is Tapu Lele, as Psychic Terrain provides Iron Crown with an immunity to priority moves from foes such as Kingambit and also boosts the power of its Psychic-type moves. In return, Iron Crown can threaten foes such as Hatterene and opposing Tapu Lele. Iron Crown struggles to beat Gholdengo, meaning Fire-type teammates that can threaten it such as Volcarona and Mega Charizard X are appreciated. In return, Iron Crown can threaten Toxapex and set up on Alomomola for them, as both of them could otherwise come in on these Fire-types comfortably. Iron Crown also struggles with Ground-types such as Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Gliscor, meaning Flying-types such as Dragonite and your own Landorus-T make excellent teammates; Landorus-T also effectively damages Steel-types, making it easier for Iron Crown to sweep. Iron Crown can repay Landorus-T by breaking through Flying-types such as Zapdos and Tornadus-T, which would otherwise be able to wall it. Iron Crown struggles to beat Ting-Lu, meaning Fighting-type teammates such as Zamazenta and Iron Valiant are appreciated, with Iron Crown in return beating Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie, Clefable and Hatterene. Dark-types like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott also make great partners, with both being able to threaten Iron Crown's main answer in Gholdengo and Hisuian Samurott also setting up Spikes to let Iron Crown break teams with greater ease.

movesets.name: Assault Vest
movesets.description:
Assault Vest Iron Crown functions as a niche defensive pivot; with the item's boost, it can leverage its high Special Defense to be able to reliably switch in on and answer foes such as Tapu Lele, Raging Bolt, and Calm Mind Iron Valiant. Psychic Noise prevents healing from foes such as Zapdos, Alomomola, and Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta, which often carries Substitute. Volt Switch lets Iron Crown pivot out of bad matchups while also having the bonus of hitting foes such as Moltres and Corviknight decently hard. Focus Blast is used to hit Steel-type targets such as Ferrothorn and Heatran for meaningful damage. On Electric Terrain teams, an EV spread with 172 Special Attack EVs can be used in order to grant Iron Crown with a Speed boost under Electric Terrain courtesy of Quark Drive, letting it outspeed the entirety of the unboosted tier.

Assault Vest Iron Crown fits primarily on bulky offense and offense teams, where its ability to check foes such as Tapu Lele and special Iron Valiant is greatly appreciated. Teammates that are vulnerable to the aforementioned Fairy-types, such as Dragonite, Garchomp, and Hisuian Samurott, all value Iron Crown's defensive capabilities. In return, all three can effectively pressure opposing Steel-types such as Heatran and Gholdengo. Iron Crown struggles with Ground-type foes such as Garchomp, Landorus-T, and Gliscor, meaning Flying-type teammates such as Zapdos and Moltres are appreciated. In return, Iron Crown can be a good switch-in against Electric-types such as Raging Bolt and Tapu Koko, which could otherwise threaten them. Iron Crown also struggles to break bulky Dark-types such as Ting-Lu; therefore, Fighting-types like Zamazenta, Iron Valiant and Urshifu-R can make good teammates. Iron Crown can support them by being a reliable answer to Psychic- and Fairy-types, including the aforementioned Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant, as well as pivoting them in against Steel-types such as Ferrothorn. Tapu Koko can also make an excellent partner due to its ability to set Electric Terrain, allowing Iron Crown to be able to outspeed and threaten foes such as Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Zamazenta, while also forming a pivoting core with it. Landorus-T and Great Tusk also form an excellent defensive core with Iron Crown, with Iron Crown being able to switch in on threats such as Tapu Lele and, in turn, these allies being good answers to common Ground-types such as Gliscor and opposing Landorus-T.

movesets.name: Calm Mind (Psychic)
movesets.description: Iron Crown charges into battle on offensive Psychic teams as a threatening Calm Mind setup sweeper with a useful defensive typing and decent bulk. With Calm Mind, Agility, and Stored Power, Iron Crown can quickly snowball out of control and muscle its way through Psychic-resistant foes while outrunning would-be revenge killers such as Meowscarada and Landorus-I. Weakness Policy is Iron Crown's preferred item, as activating it hugely increases Stored Power's Base Power without requiring multiple turns of setup. Once boosted, Iron Crown can easily use Tachyon Cutter to trample Steel-weak teams like Fairy, Rock, and Ice, while Stored Power blasts through teams typically lacking specially bulky Psychic-resistant or -immune Pokemon like Electric and Ground lacking Ting-Lu. Focus Blast can lure specially defensive phazers that usually stop Iron Crown like Ting-Lu, Hisuian Goodra, and Empoleon. Iron Crown's EVs allow it to activate Speed Quark Drive in Electric Terrain, which is very useful to outspeed fast Electric types like Tapu Koko and Zeraora that typically use Electric-type attacks freely against Psychic teams. Iron Crown greatly appreciates dual screens support, so a dedicated setter like Deoxys-S is a great help. With dual screens active, Iron Crown can survive and activate Weakness Policy against dangerous attacks like Gholdengo's Never-Ending Nightmare, Mega Charizard Y's Flamethrower, and Choice Band Excadrill's Earthquake. Tapu Lele is another notable partner, as it provides Psychic Terrain, blocking dangerous priority moves that could threaten Iron Crown like Sucker Punch and Shadow Sneak. In return, Iron Crown provides a switch-in to Poison-type moves targeting Tapu Lele and helps break through shared checks like Alolan Muk. Mega Gallade is another synergistic teammate that clobbers threats to Iron Crown like Hisuian Goodra, Blissey, Hisuian Samurott, and Bisharp. In turn, Iron Crown can break through physical walls that frustrate Mega Gallade like Dondozo, Quagsire, and Slowbro. Latias, sporting a Ground immunity and a Fire-type resistance, can not only cover these weaknesses for Iron Crown, but also can utilize Healing Wish to get it back in the race if a previous sweep attempt was halted via damage or status.
